title: Steps to Reduce Binary String to One
description:
# Steps to Reduce Binary String to One

Given a binary string `s` representing a positive integer, repeatedly apply the following rules until the value becomes exactly `1`:

* if the current value is even, divide it by `2`;
* if the current value is odd and greater than `1`, add `1`.

Return the number of operations performed. The input can be much longer than a machine integer, so solutions should reason about the binary string instead of relying on fixed-width numeric conversion.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s = "1101"
**Output:** 6
**Explanation:** 13 -> 14 -> 7 -> 8 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1.

## Example 2:

**Input:** s = "10"
**Output:** 1
**Explanation:** 2 is even, so one division reaches 1.

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= s.length <= 500`
*   `s` contains only the characters `0` and `1`.
*   `s` represents a positive integer.
*   `s` has no leading zero unless `s == "1"`.

tests.description: canonical mixed odd and even sequence
smallest odd value greater than one
carry turns all lower ones into a power of two
carry propagates through a mixed suffix
trailing one after a long zero gap
long power of two within the string-size constraint

solutions.name: Least-Significant Carry Scan
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan from the least significant bit toward the leading bit while carrying the effect of prior odd `+1` operations. Every processed lower bit must eventually be removed by one division; when its effective bit is odd, we also count the add-one operation and keep a carry for the remaining prefix.

## Key Insight

The actual value can grow beyond the original length by at most one leading carry, so the whole process is captured by a single `carry` flag. For a lower bit, effective `0` or `2` costs one division, while effective `1` costs add-one plus division.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)
solutions.code: class Solution { public int numSteps(String s) { int steps = 0; int carry = 0; for (int i = s.length() - 1; i > 0; i--) { int bit = s.charAt(i) - '0' + carry; if ((bit & 1) == 0) { steps++; } else { steps += 2; carry = 1; } } return steps + carry; } }

solutions.name: First-Carry Cost Formula
solutions.description:
## Approach

Separate the suffix before the first lower `1` from the prefix after carry starts. Trailing zeros before that first lower `1` only divide away. The first lower `1` costs add-one plus divide, then carry stays active: each remaining `0` costs two operations and each remaining `1` costs one.

## Key Insight

There is a single phase change. Before the first lower `1`, no addition has happened. After it, carry is permanent until the leading bit, because every future effective prefix is the original bit plus one pending carry.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)
solutions.code: class Solution { public int numSteps(String s) { int i = s.length() - 1; int steps = 0; while (i > 0 && s.charAt(i) == '0') { steps++; i--; } if (i == 0) return steps; steps += 2; i--; while (i > 0) { steps += s.charAt(i) == '0' ? 2 : 1; i--; } return steps + 1; } }

solutions.name: Two-State Carry Dynamic Program
solutions.description:
## Approach

Model the reduction as a two-state automaton over suffixes. `noCarry` is the cost after processing the suffix when no carry reaches the current bit; `carry` is the cost when one carry reaches it. Each new bit deterministically transitions to the next carry state with either one or two operations.

## Key Insight

This makes the invariant explicit for teaching: the entire unprocessed prefix only needs to know whether the processed suffix generated a carry. The final leading bit contributes zero extra steps without carry, or one final division if carry turns it into binary `10`.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)
solutions.code: class Solution { public int numSteps(String s) { int inf = 1_000_000; int noCarry = 0; int carry = inf; for (int i = s.length() - 1; i > 0; i--) { int bit = s.charAt(i) - '0'; int nextNoCarry = inf; int nextCarry = inf; if (noCarry < inf) { if (bit == 0) nextNoCarry = Math.min(nextNoCarry, noCarry + 1); else nextCarry = Math.min(nextCarry, noCarry + 2); } if (carry < inf) { if (bit == 0) nextCarry = Math.min(nextCarry, carry + 2); else nextCarry = Math.min(nextCarry, carry + 1); } noCarry = nextNoCarry; carry = nextCarry; } return Math.min(noCarry, carry + 1); } }

solutions.name: BigInteger Rule Simulation
solutions.description:
## Approach

Parse the binary string into a big integer and simulate the statement literally: test oddness, add one when odd, otherwise divide by two. This is not the intended fastest route, but it is a valuable executable baseline for validating the string-only reasoning.

## Key Insight

The baseline keeps the problem semantics visible. It also demonstrates why fixed-width integer conversion is not acceptable: the constraint allows hundreds of bits, so any numeric simulation must use arbitrary precision.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
solutions.code: class Solution { public int numSteps(String s) { java.math.BigInteger value = new java.math.BigInteger(s, 2); java.math.BigInteger one = java.math.BigInteger.ONE; java.math.BigInteger two = java.math.BigInteger.TWO; int steps = 0; while (!value.equals(one)) { if (value.testBit(0)) value = value.add(one); else value = value.divide(two); steps++; } return steps; } }

solutions.name: Mutable Binary String Simulation
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep the current value in a mutable binary string. A trailing zero is removed to represent division by two. A trailing one triggers manual binary add-one, flipping trailing ones to zero until a zero can become one or a new leading one is inserted.

## Key Insight

This route shows the mechanical reason behind carry propagation. It is slower because a single add-one can scan many trailing ones, but it is useful for connecting the optimized carry count to the actual binary operation.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
solutions.code: class Solution { public int numSteps(String s) { StringBuilder value = new StringBuilder(s); int steps = 0; while (!(value.length() == 1 && value.charAt(0) == '1')) { if (value.charAt(value.length() - 1) == '0') { value.deleteCharAt(value.length() - 1); } else { addOne(value); } steps++; } return steps; } private void addOne(StringBuilder value) { int i = value.length() - 1; while (i >= 0 && value.charAt(i) == '1') { value.setCharAt(i, '0'); i--; } if (i < 0) value.insert(0, '1'); else value.setCharAt(i, '1'); } }
